findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mold to be present at mop sink caulking. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring caulking at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. 

An employee was observed to don gloves and begin food handling without washing their hands. Education conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure education trickles down to all staff moving forward. Ensure that employees wash their hands at all times that it is required while preparing foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Encrusted residue is observed on the cut bar of the rack used for distributing the paper used for wrapping sandwiches. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean it and maintain it clean to protect the food contact surfaces moving forward. The item was cleaned during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

During this inspection a storm came through the area and water began leaking from the air ducts in the customer seating area. Repair prior to the next routine inspection. Maintain the facility in a state of good repair at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled during this inspection. The nozzles were disassembled and cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The prep cooler next to where orders are taken is consistently holding foods between 48F-52F. TCS items in this cooler were removed/discarded and the cooler was placed on time control until repairs can be completed. The same gentleman that will repair this cooler is already coming to this facility for another matter this evening and can work on it tonight per the owner. The inspector’s card was given and contact requested with an update when known. The current follow up will be Monday.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

1) There is a crack in the caulking between the wall and hand sink as you walk into the back hallway. The PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. 2) The magnetic rack used for storing knives above the three part sink has bare wood observed. Reseal prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

During this inspection multiple food handler cards are observed expired. Other current employees do not appear to have food handler training completed. Ensure that food handler training is completed for all employees that handle food or food contact items. The PIC looked up courses during this inspection with the inspector present.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sink and the sani buckets in the facility are observed at either low concentrations or a concentration of 0 during this inspection. The buckets and sink were remade during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mop is observed stored with the head pooled up in the bottom of the mop sink. The PIC was consulted and re-positioned the mop to correct the violation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed to wash hands then turn faucet off without using a barrier to prevent recontaminating hands. CORRECTED- Provided education and reviewed proper handwashing.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Nozzles on the soda fountain observed to have build-up inside. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who cleaned nozzles. Discussed getting them on a cleaning schedule to maintain clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Pizza sauce hot held on the flat top observed at 120F (probed). CORRECTED- Sauce reheated. Discussed hot holding temperatures and strategies to hold temperature (keeping a lid on when not in use, stirring to distribute heat). 
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employees don gloves without first washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Staff washed hands before putting on gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. (P)

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed clean potatoes stored in the cardboard boxes they were delivered in. Store produce in clean, smooth/easily cleanable containers after it is washed.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶¶ (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD (1) In a clean, dry location; and (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. (C)

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed blanched fries out and no time control policy set in place. A time control policy was completed during the inspection and must be implemented within the establishment.
750-100 Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed a prep cooler measuring 56 F (probed). The air temperature and the food was 56F.  Cheese, bacon, mayo, honey mustard and 1000 island dressings were all discarded during the inspection. The manager stated they had been having problems with the cooler. Continue to monitor and fix the cooler to maintain a temperature of 41 F or below.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored on counter tops. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer buckets to ensure proper sanitation.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the shelves holding the liquid butter to be soiled and dripping onto the boxes of potatoes. Clean the shelves. 2) Observed inside the fryers to be soiled. Clean the fryers.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a sanitizer bucket stored above potato boxes. This is not a proper practice. Sanitizer buckets and chemicals shall be stored separate from food.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed the water filter system to have an accumulation of mold in them. Ensure that the filters are regularly changed. Manager will contact owner to have them changed.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee wash their hands, then turn the faucet off without a barrier. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid recontaminating their hands. Employee was educated and they rewashed their hands. 
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the table below the flat top to have an excessive accumulation of food debris. Ensure that this table is regularly cleaned to assist in reducing drain fly populations.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the area below the soda syrup rack to have a thick accumulation of soda syrup and other food debris. Employee cleaned this area during the inspection. Ensure these floor areas are kept in a clean state to help in reducing drain fly populations. 
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to have 1 IDPH licensed FSSMC. There is now another employee with their FSSMC, but they do not have the IDPH license. After discussing it with Kevin Dreesman, the violation will be continued until there are enough IDPH licensed FSSMC for every shift. As stated last time, a minimum of 3 should be achieved. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility has one IDPH licensed FSSMC and that is the owner. The GM is still working on obtaining his IDPH license and states the owner will be putting the assistant manager through the FSSMC. If the owner is not within the premises on a regular basis, then there should be a sufficient amount of employees that have obtained the IDPH FSSMC to cover all shifts.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed 8 drain flies and other flying around the prep sink and the prep sink drain. The drains have been sufficiently cleaned, but the issue is persisting. Further measures should be taken to control the drain flies. Ensure that the further measures are taken to effectively minimize their presence. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility has one IDPH licensed FSSMC and that is the owner. The GM is still working on obtaining his IDPH license and states the owner will be putting the assistant manager through the FSSMC. If the owner is not within the premises on a regular basis, then there should be a sufficient amount of employees that have obtained the IDPH FSSMC to cover all shifts.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
GM does not have IDPH issued FSSMC and unable to verify FSSMC certificate. No other FSSMC on site during follow up inspection. Ensure that the facility maintains at least 1 FSSMC on site during all hours of food service/prep. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed two boxes of onions on the prep line that were beginning to spoil (darkened color and degradation noted). One of the onions also had an approximate 6 inch sprout coming through the apex of it. Ensure that food is maintained free of spoilage and safe for human consumption. The manager discarded the spoiled onions during the inspection.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed two bulk powders on a shelf in the dry storage area that were without labels. Ensure that bulk powders, that are not being stored in their original container, are properly labeled to ensure their identity is known. Label the powders.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed chicken salad in a prep cooler, that the manager stated was from yesterday, with no date marking. Ensure that PHFs are date marked and disposed of after 7 days. Manager was allowed to date mark the product during the inspection.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed tongs for raw chicken at the prep cooler closest to the entrance to be being stored with the handle resting in the raw chicken. Ensure that when storing utensils in food that the below measures are taken to prevent potentials for cross contamination. 
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee switching between tasks (preparing food, moving dirty dishes, and other tasks) and changing his gloves, but the employee did not wash his hands in between the changing of gloves. Any time that gloves are removed the employee's hands may become contaminated. The employee should wash their hands prior to donning a new pair of gloves. Employee was stopped and educated. Employee washed their hands and then returned to work.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed personal items being stored on top of soda syrup boxes and the soda syrup lines. Drinks were with and without lids. Ensure that if a drink is being consumed in the kitchen that it has a lid and straw. When storing personal drinks, ensure that they are stored below and away from food and drinks for service. This assists in preventing potentials for cross-contamination. Manager moved the drinks during the inspection.
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed a cabinet in the rear of the facility to have exposed bare wood. Ensure that if there is wood within the facility that it is sealed or painted to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 2) Observed the cooler, under the lemonade machine, to have a shelf that was beginning to fall of its ledge. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
GM stated the facility did not have any test strips to monitor sanitizer levels. Inspector provided a container of test strips to the facility to ensure that proper sanitizers were made for cleaning surfaces and dishes. Ensure that a test kit is regularly provided to monitor sanitizer levels. 
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed the three compartment sink to be prepared for dish washing, while food service was occurring. During the inspection, it was noted that a pitcher had been washed and was sitting in the sanitizer. Upon testing the sanitizer (Cl) it had no detectable levels. Manager informed the inspector that they had no test strips in the facility (see violation 17) to assist in preparing the solution. (See Violation 21, no sanitizer available throughout the facility.) Manager remade the sanitizer solution in the sink with bleach to a 50 ppm concentration. Ensure that when dish washing is occurring there is a proper level of sanitizer in the sink. 
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed a wet cloth sitting on a rack designated for chemicals. Ensure that wet cloths are stored, fully submerged, in a sanitizer solution when not in use. Manager moved the rag during the inspection. 2) Observed 4 separate sanitizer buckets to have no detectable levels of sanitizer. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are tested before placing them out for service and that they are changed at regular intervals. Manager was asked to make new sanitizer buckets during the inspection due to lack of sanitizer throughout the inspection. Manager was further educated on proper concentrations for Cl and proper ways to make sanitizer from bleach.  
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the potato bin that stores bulk potatoes to have an excess accumulation of old debris. The general surface of this bin appeared to be dirty. Ensure that food contact surfaces are regularly cleaned. 2) Observed an employee move the dirty dishes on a prep sink to the three compartment. Then, employee began food prep within the prep sink. Ensure that when switching the prep sink between dish sink and prep sink that it is washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Employee ceased food prep and properly cleaned the prep sink.  
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the trash cans in the rear of the facility, that are meant for dirty laundry, to be soiled with food splash on the lids. 2) Observed the lower shelf of the flat top to have an excessive accumulation of splash and debris. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service containers, next to the register, stored with the food contact surface side up with no cover. Manager was educated on proper means of storing single service. 
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed a single service sauerkraut bucket under the flat top being used to hold burnt pieces from off the grill. While this is not reuse for other food items it was still a concern based on the fact that the buckets are not emptied regularly. Per the manager, the bucket maybe emptied once every 2-3 days, unless it becomes excessively full. Cease this practice. It is recommended that use of the trash cans is exercised to ensure that waste is disposed of regularly. 
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the dumpster to be open at the time of the inspection. Ensure that the dumpster is properly maintained and shut after each use. 
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed multitudinous drain flies throughout the facility (6+) that were along the 3 compartment sink, prep sink, and prep line areas. Employee stated he had noticed them for a couple weeks. (See violation 36) Ensure that effective measures are taken to prevent pest infestations. Franchisee stated Orkin was their pest control and that she would contact them immediately. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door to have a gap at the base of the door. The weather stripping appears to be worn down. Ensure that the door is repaired to provide adequate protection to the outer opening. 
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the following floors to be soiled or in disrepair: 1) The back corner, near the laundry containers, is soiled with debris and food splatter. 2) The drains underneath the 3 compartment sink and prep sink are excessively soiled. 3) The floors under the dry storage racks are soiled with debris. 4) The floor next to the mop sink has an excessive amount of grout missing, which is allowing for waste water to sit stagnant in it. 5) Observed the floors on the prep line, against the back wall, to be excessively soiled, specifically under the equipment. Ensure that floors are maintained in good repair, as well as in a clean state. 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following walls and attached fixtures to be in disrepair: 1) The men's bathroom near the coving has exposed dry wall and chunks missing. 2) The prep sink is removed from the wall and the caulking is torn away. 3) Observed the 3 compartment sink to have the caulking in disrepair. Ensure that these walls and attached fixtures are repaired, maintained in good repair, as well as in a lean state. Ensure the sinks are recaulked to the walls. 
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed an unlableled chemical powder (manager stated it was Spic-n-Span) being stored on a shelf. A dish had been placed on the shelf under the chemical and the chemcials were open. There was powder noted that had spilled into the dish that was used for service. Ensure that chemicals are properly labeled and stored at all times. The powder was labeled and the dish was moved and cleaned. 
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Observed no proof of FSSMC (certificate or license) within the facility. GM states that he has his, but has issues with receiving his license. He also noted he does not keep his certificate on site. (see GC for conversation with franchisee). Education also provided to the GM during the inspection on means of acquiring the FSSMC through new online system. Ensure that as a High Risk Facility that there is 1 IL licensed FSSMC on site at all times during food prep. 
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the main prep cooler cutting board to be heavily scored with deep grooves. Replace cutting board or sand down surface to allow for a smooth and easily cleanable surface free from grooves.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed the dump sink to detaching from the wall. 2) Observed the 3 pan sink to be detaching from the wall. Secure these sinks and caulk the wall to sink joint to eliminate any gaps.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Upon arrival, single staff member working, R. Conant, stated he has not received his FSSMC from IDPH, however, showed a certificate of completion from ServSafe. IDPH was contacted and stated Mr. Conant has paid his fee, however, did not complete the request form completely, therefore, was not issued his certificate. Mr. Conant was given an additional request form and instructed to send in form to IDPH as soon as possible to avoid a follow up inspection. Upon receiving FSSMC, provide card information to inspector.
750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.
Observed that there were two containers of spices (sugar, salt & spices) that were not labeled with common name of product on container.
Label containers with the common name of product on container.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
Observed that the wiping cloths were stored in a clean container of water, but the container did not contain any sanitizer in the solution.
Store wiping cloths used for wiping off tabletops, counters, and other food-contact surfaces in a solution that contains an approved germ-killing chemical, so as to minimize the potential for cross-contamination. 
CORRECTED = A new solution was made with a chlorine sanitizer, and was tested and found to be 50ppm Chlorine in solution.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
Observed that the rear hand washing sink did not have a supply of towels when the inspector arrived. 
Provide a supply of towels at each lavatory.
CORRECTED = A new roll of towels was installed in the dispenser during the inspection.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
Observed that the backsplash of the prep sink in the kitchen / storage area has pulled away from the wall.
Re-attach the sink to the wall.
Observed that there is a ceiling tile missing by the back door. 
Replace the ceiling tile.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed that prep cooler 2 was missing a thermometer.
findings.citation_text:
750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.
Provide thermometers in all refrigeration units.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the cutting board on prep cooler 2 was scored sufficiently so as to be difficult to clean. 
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.
Replace this cutting board.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed that there is a leak in the upper faucet located above the prep sink. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.
Repair the leak in faucet.
**NOTE** - The manager is aware of the leak and has repair parts ordered. Anticipate repairs to be completed within 7 days.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that the floors under the fryer and under prep cooler 3 (3 door cooler) had some spillage and debris under these areas.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 
Clean the floors.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed tongs down in the lettuce in one cooler. (corrected) Observed tongs down in the bacon up front in the cooler. (Corrected)Owner stored the tongs in between the 2 bins.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed a gap at the bottom of the door at the back of the restaurant. Seal the gap. Owner corrected by drilling another screw in the base of the door.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.
